faq.answer: No. Checks can reflect standard procedures or consequential stakes. Your initial expectations about intentions need to be considered separately from the safeguard.
faq.question: Does checking a contract mean I have low Trust?

faq.answer: The facet alone cannot establish that. Starting assumptions, verification, available evidence, and the situation all matter. Good faith can coexist with firm boundaries.
faq.question: Does strong Trust mean I am easily fooled?

faq.answer: A trait description cannot diagnose or exclude a disorder. Caution may fit the evidence. If suspicion or related distress persistently affects your life, seek qualified assessment.
faq.question: Does low Trust indicate a mental disorder?

faq.answer: No. It supports that specific agreement. Broader reliance requires relevant evidence and appropriate limits, including a separate assessment of capability.
faq.question: Should one kept promise lead to unrestricted trust?

faq.answer: No. Continued contact is your choice, informed by safety, conduct, and accountability. A general personality description cannot require reconciliation or guarantee repair.
faq.question: Must I rebuild trust after betrayal?

not_for: Do not use this page for clinical diagnosis or as the sole basis for hiring or admission.
method_boundary.summary: Use this page to understand personality concepts and examine everyday behavior. Interpret actual scores using the instrument’s scoring method, reference sample, and intended use.

sections.body:
Trust concerns a general expectation that other people mean well and that their statements are broadly credible, rather than a readiness to suspect hidden motives. It belongs to Agreeableness in the NEO/IPIP-NEO vocabulary used here.

An ambiguous interaction makes the starting point visible. If your name disappears from a draft event schedule, do you first imagine a copying error or an attempt to exclude you? Neither interpretation establishes what happened.

Stronger, weaker, and intermediate positions lie on a continuum. They do not establish intelligence, your own honesty, or whether a particular person deserves access to your money, information, or time.
sections.heading: The explanation you reach for before you know

sections.body:
A person can mean well and misunderstand an instruction. They can complete one task and be unable to handle another. You can expect good faith while requiring a clear agreement, checking important facts, or limiting the consequences of an error.

Those safeguards do not reveal a trait on their own. Reading terms may be a standard requirement; skipping a check may reflect a trivial consequence. To understand Trust, ask about expectations as well as actions.

Your own trustworthy conduct is another question. So are readiness to help and willingness to yield in conflict. [Straightforwardness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/straightforwardness) examines your communication, rather than your expectation of someone else's intentions.
sections.heading: Good intentions are not a performance guarantee

sections.body:
With a more trusting starting point, you may ask for clarification without first assuming an offense. If repeated contradictions then accumulate, the question becomes whether you are updating your interpretation. Repeatedly explaining away evidence is a behavior to examine, not an inevitable consequence of strong Trust.

With a more skeptical starting point, you may want corroboration before accepting an explanation. If supporting evidence arrives but you keep introducing a new reason to doubt it, consider what would actually change your mind. Skepticism does not establish superior accuracy.

Intermediate positions can depend on the relationship or the issue. A history of broken agreements, unequal interests, and the consequences of being wrong belong in the assessment. Different treatment of a familiar friend and a new supplier is not automatically inconsistent.
sections.heading: Different starting points create different questions

sections.body:
Imagine a volunteer event organizer sends a draft schedule without Morgan's name in the helper list. Before asking, Morgan writes down a first interpretation: perhaps an older list was copied. That note supports a benign initial expectation in this instance.

The organizer explains that an old file was used. The file history is consistent with the account, and the next draft restores the name. This supports the explanation for the omission; it does not prove the organizer's inner motives or reliability in every situation.

If omissions recur, Morgan can request a confirmation step. The same check could be used by someone who is initially trusting or someone who is initially wary. Checking the list and expecting ill intent should not be treated as the same observation.
sections.heading: An omitted name is evidence of an omission

sections.body:
Use a specific hypothesis: When a new event collaborator leaves me out of a draft and the reason is unclear, I usually first consider an innocent mistake. Observe the initial explanation, not whether the event eventually succeeds.

When a comparable omission occurs naturally, record the known facts and your first interpretation before clarification. Add later evidence separately. A clear ambiguous omission followed by an immediate suspicion of deliberate exclusion is an opportunity without the expected response. An event with no omission, or one whose cause you already know, supplies no equivalent opportunity.

A single exception does not refute usually. Similar starting assumptions across comparable situations support retaining a limited description. If the pattern occurs only with collaborators who already have a good track record, narrow its scope. If entries are written after learning the outcome, or relevant events are scarce, set the hypothesis aside. No exception found is not the same as no exception possible.
sections.heading: Record natural exceptions before the outcome is known

sections.body:
For a deliberate attempt, choose a reversible task with negligible consequences, such as asking a collaborator to check a publicly available venue opening time. Agree on the question and a time to compare the answer with the venue's published information. Do not use money, private data, account access, or valuable possessions for this exercise.

Write down your expectation about intentions separately from your expectation about task performance. Afterward, compare the agreement, the result, and any independently checkable explanation. Successful completion supports this small task; an error may concern attention, understanding, or time rather than deception.

Mark the exercise as arranged rather than naturally occurring. Evaluate whether your conclusion changed in proportion to the evidence. You need not become more trusting to benefit, and this attempt does not demonstrate personality change.
sections.heading: Try one bounded collaboration and inspect the update

sections.body:
Rebuilding trust in a particular relationship depends on what has happened, what the other person now does, and what contact you choose. A personality description cannot oblige you to restore access, reconcile, or forgive.

If betrayal or persistent suspicion causes distress, support is available without treating the issue as a trait defect. This page cannot diagnose that distress or forecast a relationship's repair. Cultural comparisons likewise require suitable language, sample, and instrument evidence rather than assumptions about one individual.
sections.heading: Past harm and present boundaries still count

sections.body:
The [official IPIP facet items](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEOFacetsKey.htm) cover good intentions, credibility, and suspicion of hidden motives. The [correspondence table](https://ipip.ori.org/newNEO_FacetsTable.htm) relates the scale to NEO Trust. These are construct materials, not a test of fraud detection.

The [IPIP inventory guide](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm) distinguishes inventories measuring similar constructs. This page does not make different instruments' scores interchangeable, supply unmeasured facets, or establish a percentile conversion.

Read [Agreeableness](/en/personality/big-five/agreeableness) for the broader interpersonal context, [Altruism](/en/personality/big-five/facets/altruism) for readiness to help, and [Compliance](/en/personality/big-five/facets/compliance) for responses to conflict.
